text: 🏥🇲🇽 "The goal: free healthcare for every Mexican — medicines in every clinic and hospital, doctors, nurses. That's where we're headed." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Ciudad Madero, Tamaulipas Sheinbaum closed her Tamaulipas tour inaugurating the Ciudad Madero IMSS Bienestar General Hospital — the 32nd hospital opened since she took office. She laid out the path to a Universal Health Service: anyone will be able to be treated at IMSS, ISSSTE or IMSS Bienestar, whichever is closest, regardless of affiliation.
📸 Inauguración del Hospital General ISSSTE — Tampico, Tamaulipas, 15 de agosto de 2026

🇲🇽📰 MEXICO THIS WEEKEND — AUG 15–16 · Tamaulipas tour: Sheinbaum closed a four-city swing — Reynosa, Matamoros, Ciudad Victoria, Tampico — delivering Bienestar housing (84,000+ families statewide via FOVISSSTE/Conavi), Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro job placements, and the new ISSSTE General Hospital in Tampico. · "A visa does not define a person": her line in Tampico, to loud cheers — conviction in sovereignty, and that in Mexico no one outranks the people. · Universal Health Service: nationwide registration for the Servicio Universal de Salud credential ran Aug 10–15, reopening sign-up for ages 30–64 tied to the Pensión Bienestar.

🇲🇽🌎 "Without sovereignty, they would have imposed the privatization of health care from abroad." "A gallbladder surgery at market price costs about 150,000 pesos. A heart surgery, 700,000. A spine surgery, 600,000. Without sovereignty, they probably would have imposed health privatization from the outside." — Martí Batres, ISSSTE director, in Tampico Batres spoke at the inauguration of the ISSSTE General Hospital in Tampico, which opens with 35 specialties and adds imaging, surgery, chemotherapy and a blood bank in the coming weeks.

🇲🇽🏥 36 neoliberal years: 1,664 ISSSTE beds. The 4T: over 2,000 in two terms. "In 36 years the ISSSTE grew by barely a thousand beds — 1,600 beds. But the population grew, the number of state workers grew, and the hospitals stayed the same." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Tampico The new Tampico hospital replaces the old ISSSTE unit: from 103 to 250 beds, 20 to 37 consult rooms, a pharmacy 10 times larger. ISSSTE director Martí Batres: six neoliberal terms built 1,664 beds; the Fourth Transformation will add more than 2,000.

🇲🇽✊ Health care is a right, not a privilege. "The problem is when private replaces public — then access to health becomes a privilege, not a right. Because it's for those who have money, not for those who have the least." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Tampico Sheinbaum inaugurated the new ISSSTE General Hospital in Tampico, Tamaulipas: 250 beds, 37 specialty consult rooms, MRI, hemodynamics and dialysis — free, public care.
banner: "HEALTH IS A RIGHT, NOT A PRIVILEGE"

text:
🇲🇽📉 <u>MEXICAN STOCK EXCHANGE POSTS THIRD STRAIGHT LOSS, NEAR YEAR'S LOW</u>

The S&P/BMV IPC fell 0.66% on Friday to 64,397.45 points — its third consecutive daily loss and fourth in five sessions — leaving its 2026 gain at just 0.14%, El Economista reports. Airport operator OMA led the decline (-4.11%), followed by Qualitas (-3.45%) and Orbia (-3.37%), in a market turned cautious over the war in Iran.
banner: BMV: THIRD STRAIGHT LOSS, NEAR LOW

🇲🇽🌡️ <u>CDMX DEPLOYS DATA LAB AGAINST EXTREME HEAT, PILOT IN IZTAPALAPA</u>

Mexico City's environment ministry (SEDEMA) and WRI Mexico launched the Cool Cities Lab to map heat risk with high-precision geographic data and turn it into prevention programs, with Iztapalapa as the pilot borough. "Extreme heat has become one of the main climate risks in Mexico City," said SEDEMA climate director Ana Mendívil. The city's Climate Action Program projects temperature increases above 2°C by mid-century.
banner: CDMX FIGHTS EXTREME HEAT WITH DATA

🇲🇽♀️ <u>UN NAMES VIOLENCE AGAINST MOTHERS — MEXICO'S SEARCHING MOTHERS ARE IN THE REPORT</u>

A new UN report by Special Rapporteur Reem Alsalem recognizes violence and discrimination against mothers as a specific form of abuse — and explicitly names Mexico's madres buscadoras, women who face threats and harassment for searching for their disappeared children. The data behind it: women do 2.5 times more unpaid care work than men, 800 million lack economic security around childbirth, and 1 in 4 leave the labor market in their first year of motherhood.

🇲🇽📚 <u>MEXICO'S ANSWER TO SCREEN ADDICTION: PAUSE, THINK, READ</u>

At the president's morning press conference, education researcher Yarenia Analí Domínguez Delgado laid out the thinking behind Mexico's push for reading and phone limits in schools: "The challenge for our schools is not to compete with the speed of the screens." Her formula for the classroom: resistance, care and community — recovering attention and human bonds instead of delegating thinking to algorithms. "Learning doesn't always require more stimuli; sometimes it requires us to stop and think."
